title: Bengal to fill 27,556 government posts, Adhikari says as new police sub-inspectors join
dek: The chief minister promised a recruitment process nobody would need to challenge in court, after years in which Bengal's job drives were stalled by litigation.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal will recruit 27,556 people to government posts approved by the state Cabinet, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said in Kolkata on Saturday, promising a "fair and transparent" process that would leave no one needing to go to court.

Mr Adhikari made the announcement at a ceremony where newly recruited police sub-inspectors received their appointment letters, according to reports. He said recruitment "will not be limited to the police", naming the Forest Department among the departments where appointments would follow, and said more recruitment drives would be held in the coming months.

## What the chief minister said

"We will ensure that no one has to approach the court over recruitment-related issues," Mr Adhikari said, according to reports. He said rules for fair recruitment would be announced, without giving a date, and that age limits would be relaxed in certain cases. The government has not published a department-wise breakdown of the 27,556 posts, a timetable, or which recruiting bodies will conduct the examinations.

He said recruitment had been held up by a dispute over Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservation, and that his government had amended the OBC rules and withdrawn from the related case in the Supreme Court. He compared Bengal's police strength with Uttar Pradesh, where, he said, 90,000 constables had been recruited.

On policing, he said Kolkata Police would assess what the 112 emergency helpline needed and set a target response time of six minutes. He said he would meet Indian Police Service and Indian Forest Service officers on 13 November, and that a second agreement on police training would be signed that day, following one already signed with a national university and a police training institute in Assam. Cooperative officers recruited by the state received their appointment letters two days earlier, he said.

## Background

Government recruitment in Bengal has been tied up in the courts for years. In April 2025 the Supreme Court upheld the Calcutta High Court's cancellation of about 25,000 school teaching and non-teaching jobs filled through the West Bengal School Service Commission's 2016 examination, finding the process had been compromised. Fresh examinations for those posts have run through 2025 and 2026, and staff from the 2016 panel who were not found to be tainted are still contesting age and eligibility rules.

The state's OBC list has also been in court: in May 2024 the Calcutta High Court struck down OBC certificates issued to dozens of communities since 2010, a ruling the previous Trinamool Congress government challenged in the Supreme Court. The legal uncertainty slowed recruitment across departments that reserve posts for OBCs.

The BJP, which won the Assembly election in May and ended 15 years of Trinamool rule, made jobs and clean recruitment a central campaign promise. No response from the Trinamool Congress to Saturday's announcement had been reported by the afternoon.

## What happens next

The government is expected to notify the recruitment rules and the departments' vacancies. Mr Adhikari's meetings with IPS and IFS officers and the second police-training agreement are due on 13 November.
